item.title: Inverness Archive Project To Honour Fraser Mackintosh Legacy
item.description: A new Invernessiana archive project led by UHI Inverness will digitise and conserve 100 items from Charles Fraser Mackintosh’s collection, marking 150 years since his historic publication and inviting community volunteers to take part.The post Inverness Archive Project To Honour Fraser Mackintosh Legacy appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Salmon Firm Steps in to Restore Gigha Ferry Lights
item.description: Bakkafrost Scotland has restored navigational lights at Ardminish Bay pontoon after ferry sailings to Gigha were reduced, helping secure a vital transport link for islanders and pledging further support for emergency services access.The post Salmon Firm Steps in to Restore Gigha Ferry Lights appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: 50,000 Households Supported Through Warmer Homes Scotland
item.description: More than 50,000 households across Scotland have received support through Warmer Homes Scotland since 2015, with £400 million invested to tackle fuel poverty and improve energy efficiency in homes nationwide.The post 50,000 Households Supported Through Warmer Homes Scotland appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Plastic Wet Wipes to be Banned Across Scotland
item.description: Wet wipes containing plastic will be banned in Scotland from 11th of August 2027, following overwhelming public support and growing concern over marine litter, microplastics and sewer blockages linked to improper disposal.The post Plastic Wet Wipes to be Banned Across Scotland appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Motorcyclists Urged to Sign Up for 2026 Rider Refinement Courses
item.description: Motorcyclists across Scotland are being urged to sign up for Rider Refinement courses in 2026 after figures showed riders accounted for 18% of road deaths, despite making up less than 1% of traffic.The post Motorcyclists Urged to Sign Up for 2026 Rider Refinement Courses appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Air Discount Scheme Extended to Support Island Communities
item.description: The Air Discount Scheme has been extended until at least March 2027, continuing 50% discounted air fares for residents in parts of the Highlands and Islands to help tackle high travel costs and improve connectivity.The post Air Discount Scheme Extended to Support Island Communities appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Orkney Labour Candidate Criticises Cut to Wave Energy Scotland Funding
item.description: Orkney Labour candidate Mike Macleod has criticised the Scottish Government’s decision to terminate funding for Wave Energy Scotland, warning of potential job losses and risks to Scotland’s role in marine energy development.The post Orkney Labour Candidate Criticises Cut to Wave Energy Scotland Funding appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Orbital Marine Power Secures New UK Contract and Expands Global Pipeline
item.description: Orbital Marine Power has secured a new UK Contract for Difference award, expanding its project portfolio to 17MW and strengthening its global tidal energy pipeline across the UK and Canada.The post Orbital Marine Power Secures New UK Contract and Expands Global Pipeline appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Orbex Releases Unseen Prime Images as Administration Looms
item.description: Orbex has released unseen images of its Prime microlauncher in near flight configuration as the company prepares to enter administration, highlighting the progress made ahead of planned UK test launches.The post Orbex Releases Unseen Prime Images as Administration Looms appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Angus MacNeil Named as ALBA Highlands and Islands Lead Candidate
item.description: Angus Brendan MacNeil has been confirmed as ALBA’s lead candidate for the Highlands and Islands Regional List, setting out his party’s strategy ahead of the next Scottish Parliament election.The post Angus MacNeil Named as ALBA Highlands and Islands Lead Candidate appeared first on The Highland Times.
